\begin{table*}[!t]
\caption{Summary of sample complexity results for convex/PL functions.}
\label{table:1+}
\begin{center}
\resizebox{0.95\textwidth}{!}{
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
Method &  $\nabla f_i$ &  Convex  & PL condition & Additional Assumptions   \\
\midrule
Theorem~\ref{thm:4} & non-linear   & $\mathcal{O}\left( \epsilon^{-3}\right)$ & $\mathcal{O}\left(\mu^{-2} \epsilon^{-1}\right)$ & Average smoothness \\
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
& linear & $\mathcal{O}\left( \epsilon^{-2}\right)$ & $\mathcal{O}\left(\mu^{-1}\epsilon^{-1}\right)$ &   Average smoothness 
  \\
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
& linear  & $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \sqrt{mn} \epsilon^{-1}\right)$ & $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \sqrt{mn} \mu^{-1}\right)$  & Finite-sum structure    \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{center}
\end{table*}
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:main0}
If $g_i(\mathbf{w})$ is $C_g$-Lipschitz continuous. Setting $\gamma_{t} = 0$, and $\beta_{t} = \beta < 1$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{split}
        \mathbb{E} \left[ \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^2 \right] \leq \left(1-\frac{\beta B_1}{2m} \right)\mathbb{E} \left[\left\| \mathbf{u}_{t-1} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t-1})\right\|^2 \right] 
          + B_1 \sigma^2 \beta^2+\frac{5 m^2 C_g^2}{\beta B_1} \mathbb{E} \left[\left\| \mathbf{w}_{t} -\mathbf{w}_{t-1}\right\|^2\right]. 
        \end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
By setting the hyper-parameter $\beta$ and the learning rate $\eta_t$ appropriately, we can ensure that the function estimation error $\mathbb{E} [\left\| \mathbf{u}_{t} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^2]$ decreases gradually. However, the bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:main0} contains the $1/\beta$ factor multiplying $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathbf{w}_t-\mathbf{w}_{t-1}\|^2]$, which leads to weaker rates and motivates a variance reduction correction.
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:main1}
Suppose that $g_i(\mathbf{w}_t;\xi_t^i)$ is $C_g$-Lipschitz continuous. By setting that $\gamma_{t} = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta_{t})}+(1-\beta_{t})$, for $\beta_{t} \leq \frac{1}{2}$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t}-g\left(\mathbf{w}_{t}\right)\right\|^{2}\right]  \leq \left(1-\frac{B_1\beta_{t}}{m}\right)\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t-1}-g\left(\mathbf{w}_{t-1}\right)\right\|^{2}\right]+2B_1\beta_{t}^{2} \sigma^{2}\\
+\frac{13 m^{2} C_g^2}{B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{w}_{t}-\mathbf{w}_{t-1}\right\|^{2}\right].
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- head-6: body_md -->
Compared to Lemma~\ref{lem:main0} (where $\gamma_t=0$), we have eliminated the $\frac{1}{\beta_t}$ factor on the $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathbf{w}_{t}-\mathbf{w}_{t-1}\|^{2}]$ term, which allows for a much more rapid decrease in the estimation error.
<!-- end head-6 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:main3}
Suppose that $g_i(\mathbf{w}_t;\xi_t^i)$ is $L_g$-smooth. Setting $\gamma_{t} = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta_{t})}+(1-\beta_{t})$ and $\beta_t \leq 1/2$, we have:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^2\right] 
\leq &\left(1 - \frac{B_1\beta_{t}}{m}\right)\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t-1}- g(\mathbf{w}_{t-1})\right\|^2\right] + 2B_1\beta_{t}^2\sigma^2 \\ 
+ &\left(\frac{4 L_g^2}{\beta_{t} } \|\mathbf{w}_{t} - \mathbf{w}_{t-1}\|^2 + 9 C_g^2 +{8 \sigma^2}\right)\frac{m^2}{B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{t} - \mathbf{w}_{t-1}\|^2\right].
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- head-7: body_md -->
The bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:main3} is nearly identical to that in Lemma~\ref{lem:main1}, as long as we can ensure ${\left\|\mathbf{w}_t-\mathbf{w}_{t-1}\right\|^2}/{\beta_t} = \mathcal{O}(1)$. This condition can be satisfied by using: (i) a normalization technique, i.e., $\mathbf{w}_{t+1} = \mathbf{w}_{t} - \eta \mathbf{z}_t/ \left\|\mathbf{z}_t\right\|$, with $\eta^2/\beta_t \leq \mathcal{O}(1)$; or (ii) projection operation, i.e., $\mathbf{w}_{t+1} = \mathbf{w}_{t} - \eta_t \Pi_{C_F}\left[\mathbf{z}_t\right]$, with $\eta_t^2/\beta_t \leq \mathcal{O}(1)$.
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
The sample complexity is the number of stochastic oracle queries required to find a point that satisfies $\mathbb{E} \left[\left\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w})\right\|\right] \leq \epsilon$ ($\epsilon$-stationary point) or $\mathbb{E} \left[ F(\mathbf{w})-\inf_{\mathbf{w}} F(\mathbf{w})\right] \leq \epsilon$ ($\epsilon$-optimal solution).
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- ass-1: body_md -->
\label{ass1} 
We assume that each $f_i$ is $L_f$-smooth and $C_f$-Lipschitz continuous; each $g_i$ is $L_g$-smooth and $C_g$-Lipschitz continuous; function $F$ is lower bounded by $F_{*}$.
<!-- end ass-1 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
This implies that $F$ is $C_F$-Lipschitz continuous and $L_F$-smooth, where $C_F= C_f C_g$ and $L_F = C_f^2L_g + C_g^2L_f$~\citep{Zhang2021MultiLevelCS}.
<!-- end head-8 -->
<!-- ass-2: body_md -->
\label{ass2}  (Bounded variance)
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\mathbb{E}\left[g_i(\mathbf{x};\xi_t^i)\right] = g_i(\mathbf{x}); 
	\quad&\mathbb{E}\left[\nabla g_i(\mathbf{x};\xi_t^i)\right] = \nabla g_i(\mathbf{x}); \\
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|g_{i}\left(\mathbf{x} ; \xi_t^{i}\right)-g_{i}(\mathbf{x})\right\|^{2}\right] \leq \sigma^{2}; 
\quad&\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla g_{i}\left(\mathbf{x} ; \xi_t^{i}\right)-\nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{x})\right\|^{2}\right] \leq \sigma^{2}.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end ass-2 -->
<!-- ass-3: body_md -->
\label{ass4} (Average smoothness and Lipschitz continuity)
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|g_{i}\left(\mathbf{x} ; \xi_t^{i}\right)-g_{i}\left(\mathbf{y} ; \xi_t^{i}\right)\right\|^{2}\right]  \leq C_g^{2}\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|^{2};\\
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla g_{i}\left(\mathbf{x} ; \xi_t^{i}\right)-\nabla g_{i}\left(\mathbf{y} ; \xi_t^{i}\right)\right\|^{2}\right] \leq L_g^{2}\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|^{2}.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end ass-3 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{new:1}
For our MSVRM-v1 algorithm, set that $\gamma_t = 0$, $\alpha_t = \sqrt{\frac{B_1}{T}}$ and $\eta_t = \frac{\eta}{\left\|\mathbf{z}_t\right\|}$. Under Assumptions~\ref{ass1} and \ref{ass2}, we have the following guarantees.    
\begin{compactitem}
    \item By choosing $\beta_t = \sqrt{\frac{m }{B_1 T}}$ and $\eta = \frac{B_1^{1/4}}{m^{1/4}T^{3/4}} $, we find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $  \mathcal{O}\left(m \epsilon^{-4} \right)$.
    \item If function $\nabla f_i$ is linear, by setting $\beta_t = 1$ and $\eta = \frac{B_1^{1/4}}{T^{3/4}}$, we find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $  \mathcal{O}\left(\epsilon^{-4} \right)$.
\end{compactitem}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- head-9: body_md -->
The lower bound for stochastic non-convex optimization under standard smoothness assumptions is $\Omega(\epsilon^{-4})$~\citep {Arjevani2019LowerBF}, indicating that our $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$ complexity is optimal in this setting.
<!-- end head-9 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:1}
For MSVRM-v1 method, set $\eta_t = \min\left\{\left(\frac{B_1}{m}\right)^{2/3}(a+t)^{-1/3},\sqrt{B_1}(a+t)^{-1/2}\right\}$, $\alpha_{t+1} = \mathcal{O}\left( \eta_t \right)$,  $\beta_{t+1} = \mathcal{O}( \frac{m^2 \eta_t^2}{B_1^2})$, $\gamma_{t} = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta_{t})}+(1-\beta_{t})$,  and $a = \mathcal{O}(\frac{m}{B_1})$. 
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, we can find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $  \mathcal{O}\left( {m \epsilon^{-3}}+{\epsilon^{-4}} \right)$.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:2}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, MSVRM-v2 with $\gamma_{t} = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta_{t})}+(1-\beta_{t})$, $\alpha_{t+1} = \mathcal{O}(\frac{m \eta_{t}^2}{B_1})$, $a=O(\frac{m }{B_1}$), $\eta_t = \mathcal{O}\left((\frac{B_1 }{m})^{2/3}(a+t)^{-1/3} \right)$, and $\beta_{t+1} = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{m^2 \eta_t^2}{B_1^2}\right)$,  can find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a sample complexity of $ \mathcal{O}\left({m  \epsilon^{-3}} \right)$.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- head-10: body_md -->
The proposed algorithms can also incorporate Adam-style learning rates while preserving the same complexities. The details are provided in the appendix.
<!-- end head-10 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{new:2}
For MSVRM-v2 method, set that $\eta_t = \frac{\eta}{\left\|\mathbf{z}_t\right\|}$. Under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, we have the following guarantees.
\begin{compactitem}
    \item By using that $\gamma_{t} = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta)}+(1-\beta)$, $\alpha_t = \frac{m^{2/3}B_1^{1/3}}{T^{2/3}}$, $\beta_t = \frac{m^{2/3}}{B_1^{2/3}T^{2/3}}$ and $\eta = \frac{B_1^{1/3}}{m^{1/3}T^{2/3}}$, we find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $  \mathcal{O}\left(m \epsilon^{-3} \right)$.
    \item If function $\nabla f_i$ is linear, by setting that $\gamma_t=0$, $\beta_t = 1$, $\alpha_t = \frac{B_1^{1/3}}{T^{2/3}}$, $\eta = \frac{B_1^{1/3}}{T^{2/3}}$, we find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\epsilon^{-3} \right)$.
\end{compactitem}
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- head-11: body_md -->
Compared with Theorem~\ref{thm:2}, this result does not require knowledge of problem-dependent parameters. Moreover, it removes the dependence on $m$ when $\nabla f_i$ is linear.
<!-- end head-11 -->
<!-- head-12: body_md -->
When $m=1$ and $f$ is the identity function, the problem reduces to standard stochastic  optimization. The $\Omega\left({\epsilon^{-3}}\right)$ lower bound for this class (average smoothness )~\citep{Arjevani2019LowerBF} indicates that our MSVRM-v2 complexity is optimal.
<!-- end head-12 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:main2}
By setting that $\gamma = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta)}+(1-\beta)$, $\beta \leq 1/2$ and $\beta I \leq {m}/{B_1}$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{E} \left[ \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^2 \right] \leq  \frac{15 m^3C_g^2}{B_1^2 \beta T}  \sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb{E}\left[ \left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_{t}\right\|^2\right]
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- head-13: body_md -->
Compared with Lemma~\ref{lem:main1}, we remove the $2 B_1 \beta^2 \sigma^2$ term. This is the key to improving the complexity, as it allows us to use a much larger $\beta$.
<!-- end head-13 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:3}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, our MSVRM-v3 algorithm with $I =\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{mn}{B_1 }\right)$, $\alpha = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{ B_{1} }{m n }\right)$, $\beta = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{ 1 }{n}\right)$ and $\eta = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{B_1 }{m \sqrt{n}} \right)$, finds an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a sample complexity of $ \mathcal{O}\left( {m \sqrt{n}} \epsilon^{-2} \right)$.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- head-14: body_md -->
When $m=B_1=1$ and $f$ is the identity function, problem~(\ref{p:2}) reduces to standard finite-sum optimization, i.e., $\min \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} g_{i}(\mathbf{w}; \xi_{j})$. The lower bound for this setting is $\Omega\left(\sqrt{n}\epsilon^{-2}\right)$~\citep{Fang2018SPIDERNN,pmlr-v139-li21a}, indicating that our rate is optimal in its dependence on $n$ and $\epsilon$.
<!-- end head-14 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{new:3}
For our MSVRM-v3 algorithm, set that $\eta_t = \frac{\eta}{\left\|\mathbf{z}_t\right\|}$, $I=\frac{mn}{B_1}$, $\alpha = \frac{B_1}{mn}$, $\eta = \frac{B_1^{1/2}}{m^{1/4}n^{1/4}T^{1/2}}$. Under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, we have the following guarantees.
\begin{compactitem}
    \item Choosing $\gamma = \frac{m-B_1}{B_1(1-\beta)}+(1-\beta)$ and $\beta = \frac{1}{n}$, we find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $  \mathcal{O}\left(m \sqrt{n}\epsilon^{-2} \right)$.
    \item When $\nabla f_i$ is linear, choosing $\widehat \mathbf{u}_t^i =  g_i\left(\mathbf{w}_{t}; \xi_t^{i}\right)$, we find an $\epsilon$-stationary point with a complexity of $  \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{mn}\epsilon^{-2} \right)$.
\end{compactitem}
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- head-15: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{new:3} removes reliance on problem-dependent parameters and improves the dependence on $m$ for linear $\nabla f_i$. This $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{mn})$ reliance is known to be optimal in the finite-sum settings~\citep{Fang2018SPIDERNN,pmlr-v139-li21a}.
<!-- end head-15 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
$F(\mathbf{w})$ satisfies the $\mu$-PL condition if there exists $\mu > 0$ such that for all $\mathbf{w}$:
\begin{equation*}
    2 \mu\left(F(\mathbf{w})-F_{*}\right) \leq\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w})\|^{2}. 
\end{equation*}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- head-16: body_md -->
Since $\mu$-strong convexity implies the $\mu$-PL condition~\citep{Karimi2016LinearCO}, all results under the $\mu$-PL condition apply directly to the $\mu$-strongly convex objectives.
<!-- end head-16 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
Suppose the function satisfies the $\mu$-PL condition, and  $\nabla f_i$ is linear. Assume we have $\mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{w}_{s-1}) - F_* ]\leq \epsilon_{s-1}$ and $\mathbb{E}[\left\|\mathbf{z}_{s-1}-\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{s-1})\right\|^2] \leq \mu \epsilon_{s-1}$ for stage $s-1$. By setting $\alpha_s = \mathcal{O}(B_1 \mu \epsilon_s)$, $\eta_s = \mathcal{O}(B_1 \sqrt{\mu \epsilon_s})$, $T_s = \mathcal{O}(1/(B_1 \mu \epsilon_s))$, $\gamma_s = 0$ and $\beta_s =1$, we ensure
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{w}_{s}) - F_* ]\leq \epsilon_{s} = \epsilon_{s-1}/2, \quad \mathbb{E}[\left\|\mathbf{z}_{s}-\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{s})\right\|^2] \leq \mu \epsilon_{s}= \mu\epsilon_{s-1}/2.
    \end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- head-17: body_md -->
This lemma shows that the optimal gap $\mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{w}_{s}) - F_* ]$ and the gradient estimation error $\mathbb{E}[\left\|\mathbf{z}_{s}-\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{s})\right\|^2]$ are both halved after each stage.
<!-- end head-17 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:4}
	The stage-wise MSVRM-v1, under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, derives a complexity of $\mathcal{O}(m\epsilon^{-3})$ for convex functions and  $\mathcal{O}(m\mu^{-2}\epsilon^{-1})$ for functions satisfying the $\mu$-PL condition.
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:4+}
	 The stage-wise MSVRM-v2, under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, derives a complexity of $ \mathcal{O}\left(m \epsilon^{-2} \right)$ for convex functions and $ \mathcal{O}\left({m}\mu^{-1} \epsilon^{-1} \right)$ for functions satisfying $\mu$-PL objectives.
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:6}
    The stage-wise MSVRM-v3, under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, attains a complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{m \sqrt{n} }{\epsilon B_1  } \log{\frac{1}{\epsilon}} \right)$ for convex objectives and $ \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{m \sqrt{n} }{\mu B_1   } \log{\frac{1}{\epsilon}} \right)$ for the $\mu$-PL condition functions.
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
\label{new:4}
	For stage-wise MSVRM-v1, under Assumptions~\ref{ass1} and \ref{ass2}, when $\nabla f_i$ is linear, it derives a complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-3})$ for convex functions and $\mathcal{O}(\mu^{-2}\epsilon^{-1})$ for the $\mu$-PL functions.
<!-- end thm-10 -->
<!-- thm-11: body_md -->
\label{new:5}
 For stage-wise MSVRM-v2, under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, supposing that function $\nabla f_i$ is linear, it derives a complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ for convex functions and $\mathcal{O}(\mu^{-1}\epsilon^{-1})$ for functions satisfying the $\mu$-PL condition.
<!-- end thm-11 -->
<!-- head-18: body_md -->
The above complexities are optimal, matching the $\Omega\left(\epsilon^{-2}\right)$ and $\Omega\left(\mu^{-1}\epsilon^{-1}\right)$ lower bounds for stochastic convex and strongly convex optimization~\citep{Agarwal2012InformationTheoreticLB}.
<!-- end head-18 -->
<!-- thm-12: body_md -->
\label{new:6}
    For stage-wise MSVRM-v3, under Assumptions~\ref{ass1}, \ref{ass2} and \ref{ass4}, supposing that function $\nabla f_i$ is linear, it derives a sample complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left({ \sqrt{mn} \epsilon^{-1}} \log{\frac{1}{\epsilon}} \right)$ for convex functions and $ \mathcal{O}\left({ \sqrt{mn} \mu^{-1}} \log{\frac{1}{\epsilon}} \right)$ for functions satisfying the $\mu$-PL condition.
<!-- end thm-12 -->
<!-- head-19: body_md -->
For the finite-sum PL functions, we achieve a linear convergence rate $\mathcal{O}\left( \log(1/\epsilon) \right)$, matching the SOTA results for single-level finite-sum problems~\citep{pmlr-v139-li21a}.
<!-- end head-19 -->
<!-- head-20: body_md -->
Figure~\ref{fig:1} plots the training loss versus the number of samples, averaged over 5 runs. We observe that MSVRM-v1 performs comparably to or slightly better than SOX, and MSVRM-v2 consistently converges faster than both SOX and MSVRM-v1. MSVRM-v3 shows the fastest convergence, decreasing the loss most rapidly and demonstrating its superior efficiency, which aligns with our theoretical findings. For adaptive methods~(AdaMSVRM-v1,v2,v3), they perform slightly better than the non-adaptive counterpart in most cases, validating their effectiveness in practice.
<!-- end head-20 -->
<!-- head-21: body_md -->
We compare our proposed algorithms (MSVRM-v1, v2, v3) against their variant counterparts on CIFAR100. The results are reported in Figure~\ref{fig:2}. As can be seen, all three variant methods perform worse than our original algorithms. This empirically confirms the importance of our customized error correction term, which properly handles the dual sources of randomness.
<!-- end head-21 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:2}Denote $\|\mathbf{u}_{t}  - g(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^m\|\mathbf{u}^{i}_{t}  - g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2$, $\|\mathbf{u}_{t}  - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^m\|\mathbf{u}^{i}_{t}  - \mathbf{u}^{i}_{t-1}\|^2$.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E}\left[ \|\mathbf{z}_{t+1} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{t+1})\|^2 \right] \leq (1-\alpha_{t+1}) \mathbb{E}\left[ \|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{t})\|^2 \right]+\frac{3 C \eta_t^{2} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{z}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]}{\alpha_{t+1}} \\
&\quad\quad +\frac{4 L_{f}^{2} C_{g}^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{2 \alpha_{t+1}^{2} C_{f}^{2}\left(\sigma^{2}+C_{g}^{2}\right)}{B_{1}}+ \frac{5\alpha_{t+1} L_{f}^{2} C_{g}^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^{2}\right] 
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- head-22: body_md -->
According to Lemma 9 in \citep{dependent2022}, if $\alpha \leq {2}/{7}$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E}\left[ \|\mathbf{z}_{t+1} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{t+1})\|^2 \right] \leq(1-\alpha_{t+1}) \mathbb{E}\left[ \|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{t})\|^2 \right]+{2 L_{F}^{2} \eta_t^{2} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{z}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]}/{\alpha_{t+1}} \\
&\quad +\frac{3 L_{f}^{2} C_{g}^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{2 \alpha_{t+1}^{2} C_{f}^{2}\left(\sigma^{2}+C_{g}^{2}\right)}{B_{1}}+ \frac{5\alpha_{t+1} L_{f}^{2} C_{g}^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1} - g(\mathbf{w}_{t+1})\right\|^{2}\right].
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
By setting $\alpha \leq {1}/{15}$, we have the above lemma.
<!-- end head-22 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:3} If $\beta_{t+1} \leq {1}/{2}$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
  \mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_{t}\|^2\right]   &\leq {2B_1\beta_{t+1}^{2}  \sigma^{2} }   + \frac{4B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2} }{m} \mathbb{E}\left[ \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t}- g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{9 m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\right]
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- head-23: body_md -->
Note that with $\beta_{t+1} \leq \frac{1}{2}$, we have $\gamma_{t+1} \leq \frac{2m}{B_1}$
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_t\|^2 \right] \\
=& \frac{B_1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\beta_{t+1}\left(g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1};\xi_{t+1}^i)-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{i}\right)+\gamma_{t+1}\left(g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1};\xi_{t+1}^{i})-g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t};\xi_{t+1}^{i})\right)\right\|^{2}\right] \\
\leq& \frac{B_1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \mathbb{E}\left[2\beta_{t+1}^{2} \left\|g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1};\xi_{t+1}^{i})-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{i}\right\|^{2}+2\gamma_{t+1}^{2} \|g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1};\xi_{t+1}^{i})-g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t};\xi_{t+1}^{i})\|^{2}\right] \\
\leq& \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{2B_1\beta_{t+1}^{2}}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m}  \left\|g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1};\xi_{t+1}^{i})  -\mathbf{u}_{t}^{i}\right\|^{2}+{2B_1\gamma_{t+1}^{2} C_g^2}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\right] \\
\leq& \frac{2B_1\beta_{t+1}^{2}}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \left(\mathbb{E}\left[ \left\|g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1};\xi_{t+1}^{i}) - g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1})\right\|^{2}\right]+ \mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) -\mathbf{u}_{t}^{i}\right\|^{2}\right]\right)\\
&+{2B_1\gamma_{t+1}^{2} C_g^2} \mathbb{E}\left[ \|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\right] \\
\leq& 2 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2} \sigma^{2} +\frac{2 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2}}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1})-\mathbf{u}^{i}_t\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{8m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\right] \\
\leq& 2 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2} \sigma^{2} +\frac{4 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2}}{m} \left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) - g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^{2}+\frac{4 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t})-\mathbf{u}_t\right\|^{2}\right]\\
&+\frac{8m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\right] \\
\leq& 2 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2} \sigma^{2} +\frac{4 B_1 \beta_{t+1}^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t}) - \mathbf{u}_t\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{9m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\right].
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end head-23 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:1}(Lemma 2 in \citep{pmlr-v139-li21a}) Suppose function F is ${L_F}$-smooth and consider the update $\mathbf{w}_{t+1}:=\mathbf{w}_{t}-\eta_t \mathbf{z}_{t}$. With $\eta_t L\leq \frac{1}{2}$, we have: 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
 F(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) \leq F(\mathbf{w}_t) - \frac{\eta_t}{2} \|\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2 + \frac{\eta_t}{2} \|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2 - \frac{\eta_t}{4} \left\|\mathbf{z}_t\right\|^2
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- thm-13: body_md -->
If we choose that $\alpha_{t+1} = \mathcal{O}(\frac{m \eta_{t}^2}{B_1})$, $\beta_{t+1} = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{m^2 \eta_t^2}{B_1^2}\right)$, $a=O(\frac{m }{B_1}$) and $\eta_t = \mathcal{O}\left((\frac{B_1 }{m})^{2/3}(a+t)^{-1/3} \right)$, Adam-style MSVRM-v2 with learning rate defined in (\ref{rule1}), can obtain a stationary point in $ \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{m \epsilon^{-3} }{ B_1  } \right)$ iterations.
<!-- end thm-13 -->
<!-- head-24: body_md -->
The sample complexity is still at the order of $\mathcal{O}\left(\epsilon^{-3}\right)$. For MSVR-v1 and MSVR-v3, or under the convexity or PL condition, the Adam-style method can still get the same complexity as the original rate using a very similar analysis.
<!-- end head-24 -->
<!-- head-25: body_md -->
Note that since the norm of estimated gradient $\left\| \mathbf{z}_{t} \right\|$ is bounded, the value of the learning rate scaling factor $\mathbf{c}=1 /\left(\sqrt{\mathbf{h}_{t}}+\delta\right)$ is also upper bounded and lower bounded, which can be presented as $c_{l} \leq\left\|\mathbf{c}\right\|_{\infty} \leq c_{u}$. (Note that projection onto a ball of radius $C_F$ does not change the analysis, since $\nabla F$ is also in this ball.) With this property, we have:
<!-- end head-25 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:starter_} (Lemma 3 in \citep{guo2022stochastic})
    For $\mathbf{w}_{t+1}=\mathbf{w}_{t}-\tilde{\eta}_{t} \mathbf{z}_{t}$, with $\eta_t c_{l} \leq \tilde{\eta}_{t} \leq \eta_t c_{u} $ and $ \eta_t L_F\leq {c_l}/{2 c_u^2 }$, we have following guarantee:
    \begin{align*}
        F(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) \leq F(\mathbf{w}_t) + \frac{\eta_t c_{u}}{2}\left\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t) - \mathbf{z}_t\right\|^2 - \frac{\eta_t c_{l}}{2}\left\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t)\right\|^2 - \frac{\eta_t c_{l}}{4}\left\|\mathbf{z}_t\right\|^2.
    \end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:7} If $\beta \leq \frac{1}{2}$ and $\beta I \leq \frac{m}{B_1}$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
  \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T} \|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_{t}\|^2\right]   &\leq   \frac{4B_1 \beta^{2} }{m} \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t}- g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^{2}\right] +\frac{11 m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- head-26: body_md -->
Following the analysis of Lemma~\ref{lem:3}, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_t\|^2 \right] \\
\leq& \frac{2B_1\beta^{2}}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \left(\mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| \widehat g_{i}^{t+1} - g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1})\right\|^{2}\right]+ \mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) -\mathbf{u}_{t}^{i}\right\|^{2}\right]\right)+\frac{8m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}\\ 
\leq& 2B_1\beta^{2} C_g^2\left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{\tau}\right\|^{2} + \frac{2B_1\beta^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) -\mathbf{u}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{8m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
So, with $\beta I \leq m / B_1$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{u}_{t+1}-\mathbf{u}_t\|^2 \right] \\
\leq&  \frac{2B_1\beta^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t+1}) -\mathbf{u}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]+2B_1\beta^{2} C_g^2\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{\tau}\right\|^{2} +\frac{8m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2} \\
\leq&  \frac{4B_1\beta^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t}) -\mathbf{u}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]+ 2B_1\beta^{2} C_g^2 I^2 \sum_{t=1}^T   \left\| \mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_t\right\|^2+\frac{9m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2} \\
\leq&  \frac{4B_1\beta^{2}}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\| g(\mathbf{w}_{t}) -\mathbf{u}_{t}\right\|^{2}\right]+\frac{11m^2 C_g^2}{B_1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2}
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end head-26 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:9} 
With $\alpha I \leq 1$ ,  we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
     &\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\right\|^2 \right]
    \leq  \frac{1}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2  \\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad+\frac{8C_g^2L_f^2}{mB_1 \alpha} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2 \right]+ \frac{8C_f^2 L_g^2}{ B_1\alpha}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 \right]
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- head-27: body_md -->
First, since $\mathbf{h}_t$ is an unbiased estimation of $\frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})$, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split} 
    &\mathbb{E}\left[\left\| \mathbf{h}_t - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\right\|^{2}\right]  \\
    =& \mathbb{E}\left[\left\| \frac{1}{B_1}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{1}^{t}}  \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{t-1}^{i}) \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t;\xi_t^{i}) - \frac{1}{B_1}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{1}^{t}}  \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{i}) \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{\tau};\xi_t^{i}) \right.\right. \\
    &\quad\quad\quad \left.\left. + \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}  \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{i}) \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{\tau})- \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\right\|^{2}\right] \\
    \leq& \frac{1}{B_1^2}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{1}^{t}} \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|  \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{t-1}^{i}) \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t;\xi_t^{i}) -  \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{i}) \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{\tau};\xi_t^{i}) \right\|^{2}\right]\\
    =& \frac{2C_f^2L_g^2}{B_1} \left\|\mathbf{w}_{t} -\mathbf{w}_{\tau} \right\|^{2} +  \frac{2C_g^2L_f^2}{m B_1}   \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t-1} -\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1} \right\|^{2}
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Next, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\|^2 \right]\\
=&\mathbb{E}\left[\bigg\| (1-\alpha) \left(\mathbf{z}_{t-1} -  \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t-1})\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-2})\right) + \alpha\left(\mathbf{h}_t - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1}) \right)\right.\\
&\left. + (1-\alpha)\left(\frac{1}{B_1}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{1}^{t}} \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t;\xi_t^{i}) \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{t-1}^{i})- \frac{1}{B_1}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{1}^{t}}\nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t-1};\xi_t^{i})\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{t-2}^{i})\right.\right.\\
&\left.\left. \quad\quad\quad\quad\quad  - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t})\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1}) + \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t-1})\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-2})\right)  \bigg\|^2\right]\\
& \leq \mathbb{E}\bigg[(1-\alpha)^2 \left\|\mathbf{z}_{t-1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t-1})\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-2})\right\|^2  + \frac{4\alpha^2 C_f^2L_g^2}{B_1} \left\|\mathbf{w}_{t} -\mathbf{w}_{\tau} \right\|^{2}  \\
&\quad +  \frac{4\alpha^2 C_g^2L_f^2}{m B_1}   \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t-1} -\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1} \right\|^{2} + \frac{2(1-\alpha)^2}{B_1^2}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{1}^{t}}\left\| \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t;\xi_t^{i}) \nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{t-1}^{i})- \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t-1};\xi_t^{i})\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{u}_{t-2}^{i})\right\|^2\bigg]\\
& \leq\mathbb{E}\bigg[ (1-\alpha) \|\mathbf{z}_{t-1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_{t-1})\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-2})\|^2  + \frac{4\alpha^2 C_f^2L_g^2}{B_1} \left\|\mathbf{w}_{t} -\mathbf{w}_{\tau} \right\|^{2}\\
&\quad+  \frac{4\alpha^2 C_g^2L_f^2}{mB_1}   \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t-1} -\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1} \right\|^{2}  + \frac{4C_g^2L_f^2}{mB_1} \|\mathbf{u}_{t-1} - \mathbf{u}_{t-2}\|^2 + \frac{4C_f^2 L_g^2}{B_1}\|\mathbf{w}_{t} - \mathbf{w}_{t-1}\|^2 \bigg]
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
The first inequality is due to the fact that the last two terms equal zero in expectation.

Summing up, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
    &\sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\right\|^2 \\
    \leq & \frac{1}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2  + \frac{4\alpha C_f^2L_g^2}{B_1} \sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} -\mathbf{w}_{\tau} \right\|^{2}  \\
      &+\frac{4\alpha C_g^2L_f^2}{mB_1}   \sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t} -\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1} \right\|^{2} + \frac{4C_g^2L_f^2}{m B_1\alpha} \sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2 + \frac{4C_f^2 L_g^2}{B_1 \alpha}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2  \\
        \leq & \frac{1}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2  +
      \frac{4\alpha C_f^2L_g^2 I^2}{B_1} \sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} -\mathbf{w}_{t} \right\|^{2}  \\
      &+\frac{4\alpha C_g^2L_f^2 I^2}{mB_1}   \sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{u}_{t} -\mathbf{u}_{t-1} \right\|^{2}  + \frac{4C_g^2L_f^2}{m B_1\alpha } \sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2 + \frac{4C_f^2 L_g^2}{B_1 \alpha}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2  \\
       \leq & \frac{1}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2  + \frac{8C_g^2L_f^2}{m B_1\alpha} \sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2 + \frac{8C_f^2 L_g^2}{ B_1\alpha}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
The last inequality is due to $\alpha I \leq 1$.
            

\noindent \textbf{The rest proof of Theorem~5:} 
First, we have that:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2 
&\leq 4\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigg\|\mathbf{z}_{t} -  \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\bigg\|^2 \\
&\quad + \frac{4C_g^2L_f^2}{m}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \|  \mathbf{u}_t - \mathbf{u}_{t-1} \|^2 +\frac{2 C_g^2L_f^2}{m} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\|  \mathbf{u}_t - g(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2 
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
We use Lemma~\ref{lem:9} to replace $\sum_{t=1}^T \left\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_t)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{t-1})\right\|^2$:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
    &\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2 \right] \\
    \leq& \frac{4}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2 +\frac{32C_g^2L_f^2}{m B_1\alpha} \sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2   \\
    &\quad + \frac{32C_f^2 L_g^2}{ B_1\alpha}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 + \frac{4C_g^2L_f^2}{m} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \|  \mathbf{u}_t - \mathbf{u}_{t-1} \|^2 +\frac{2 C_g^2L_f^2}{m} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\|  \mathbf{u}_t - g(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2 \\
    \leq &\frac{4}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2 +\frac{36C_g^2L_f^2}{m \alpha} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{u}_{t} - \mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2 \right]  \\
    &\quad  +\frac{32C_f^2 L_g^2}{B_1 \alpha}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 \right]+\frac{2 C_g^2L_f^2}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|  \mathbf{u}_t - g(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2 \right]
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Set $\beta B_1 \leq m \alpha$. We use Lemma~\ref{lem:7} to replace $\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T} \|\mathbf{u}_{t}-\mathbf{u}_{t-1}\|^2\right]$ (set $\mathbf{u}_0 = \mathbf{u}_1$):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
    &\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t)\|^2 \right] \\
    \leq &\frac{4}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2 + \frac{144(C_g^2L_f^2)B_1 \beta^{2}}{m^2 \alpha}\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{u}_{t}- g(\mathbf{w}_{t})\right\|^{2}\right]   \\
    & +\frac{396 m(C_g^4L_f^2)}{\alpha B_1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1}-\mathbf{w}_{t}\|^{2} + \frac{32C_f^2 L_g^2}{B_1 \alpha}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 \right] \\
    &+\frac{2 C_g^2L_f^2}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|  \mathbf{u}_t - g(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2 \right] \\
    \leq& \frac{4}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2+\frac{428 m C}{\alpha B_1}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 \right]\\
    &+\frac{146 C_g^2L_f^2}{m} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|  \mathbf{u}_t - g(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2 \right] \\
    \leq &\frac{4}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2 +\frac{428 m C}{\alpha B_1} \sum_{t=1}^T\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_t\|^2 \\
    &+ \frac{2190 m^{2} C_g^4L_f^2}{B_1^2 \beta} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_{t}\right\|^{2}\\
    \leq &\frac{4}{\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{1} - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \nabla g_{i}(\mathbf{w}_1)\nabla f_i(\mathbf{u}^i_{0})\right\|^2  +\frac{2618 m^{2} C}{B_1^2 \beta} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_{t}\right\|^{2}\\
    \leq &\frac{2618 m^{2} C}{B_1^2 \beta} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{w}_{t+1} - \mathbf{w}_{t}\right\|^{2}\\
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Set $\frac{2618 m^{2} C \eta^{2}}{B_1^2 \beta} \leq \frac{1}{2}$. We have $
    \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \|\mathbf{z}_{t} - \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_{t})\|^2 \right] \leq \frac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{t}\right\|^{2}$.
    
\noindent According to Lemma~\ref{lem:1}, we have:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
    \frac{1}{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2\right] \leq& \frac{2 F(\mathbf{w}_1)}{\eta T} + \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathbf{z}_{t}- \nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t) \|^2\right] -\frac{1}{2T} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|\mathbf{z}_{t}\right\|^{2} 
    \leq \frac{2 F(\mathbf{w}_1)}{\eta T} 
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Note that the sample complexity is $\left(B_1 T + \frac{m n T}{I}\right)$. To ensure the first term and the second term are in the same order, we set $I = \left(\frac{m n}{B_1 }\right)$. Also, since we assume that $\alpha I \leq 1$ and $\beta I \leq \frac{m}{B_1}$, we directly set $\alpha = \frac{B_1}{m n}$ and $\beta = \frac{1}{n}$. This setting also satisfies the requirement $B_1 \beta \leq m \alpha$. We also require $\frac{2618 m^2 C \eta^2}{B_1^2 \beta} \leq \frac{1}{2}$. So, we set $\eta = \mathcal{O}(\frac{B_1 }{m \sqrt{n}})$ and we can ensure that 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
    \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w}_t) \|\right] 
    \leq \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{m^{1/2}n^{1/4}}{ (B_1 T)^{1/2}}\right) 
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
